proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen claim still charges the optional structural-chart multiplier to the mandatory decision and does not state the accepted raw-fiber variable, atom, and degree counts. The replacement restricts the complexity claim to the actual two-call engine, preserves the diagnostic template bounds separately, bounds the initial sample and second-stage witness over their correct fields, and inserts the required target-sum height increment before the second call.

prose_updates.tldr: For every fixed finite four-response-type selected proxy model, PN/PS rigidity is decided directly on the raw legal cycle fiber. After the strict supplied-margin check in design A, the compiler makes one bounded-algebraic-sampling call and, when the fiber is nonempty, one one-copy unequal-target existential call. It returns incompatibility, an exact common target, or legal same-observable SCM twins. A separate exhaustive rank-two, L/R/E/D, support-face, shared-endpoint, and relevant-IV residual-forest atlas supplies optional structural labels but is not queried by the decision engine. The published regular formulas retain their existing transfer scope; the contribution is classification of additional compatible singular and boundary laws. Fixed-alphabet record and algebraic-degree bounds are singly exponential. Initial-sample degrees and second-stage degrees are controlled separately, and rational height includes the finite cost of forming the sampled target before the second call.

project_justification.niche: The four response types form a labeled causal cycle whose target can be rigid while nuisance factorizations vary. The normalized design-A and design-B legal fibers are bounded one-copy semialgebraic sets, so global constancy is decided by comparing every feasible point with one sampled target in a single existential query. The exhaustive orientation, rank-one, support-face, shared-endpoint, and residual-forest charts remain a separate exact explanation of every singular and boundary configuration.
project_justification.fill: The compiler first checks strict supplied-margin compatibility in design A, samples once from the applicable raw legal fiber, and performs one raw-fiber unequal-target test. It returns an exact target, legal target-changing full SCMs, or incompatibility. The structural atlas can label the result and retains its finite template bound, but contributes no multiplier or auxiliary variables to mandatory decision complexity. The termination theorem uses raw degree two in design A and degree three in design B, bounds initial-sample coordinates in their sampling extension, bounds a second-stage witness by the product of the sampled-target and relative existential degrees, and composes rational height after adding the binary-length cost of summing the sampled target coordinates.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The result is a theorem-level exact symbolic procedure, not a claim of a completed production implementation or favorable growing-alphabet complexity. The mandatory decision works on the raw legal fiber and makes at most one sampling and one unequal-target existential call. The finite structural atlas can be produced diagnostically but is not required for compatibility or rigidity. Over arbitrary real observables, computation is relative to effective coefficient-field arithmetic, order, sign determination, and real-root oracles. The initial sample generally belongs to its own sampling extension and is not asserted to lie in the field generated by the sampled target and a second-stage witness; the two coordinate-degree bounds are therefore proved separately. Rational height also accounts for summing up to k initial coordinates to form each target coordinate before the second-stage call. Strictly positive twins require both cycle witnesses to lie in interior support charts. The exact-coverage and locally saturated Hausdorff qualifications are unchanged. The released numerical GEUVADIS count table and binarization thresholds remain unavailable in the frozen materials, so no numerical dataset verdict is asserted.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The mathematical contribution is an exact fixed-alphabet raw-fiber rigidity decision together with a separate exhaustive response-cycle structural atlas. Design-A margins outside the strict interior and empty raw fibers are reported as incompatibility, which is non-rigid under the cardinality-one definition. One raw-fiber sample and one unequal-target existential query decide global constancy across all components and support faces; the chart atlas supplies optional diagnoses rather than a computational prerequisite. The regular two-proxy result transfers only by restricting Condition 1 to a fixed population margin, and the regular IV result transfers through equation (13) and Corollary 1; the new result adds compatible singular and boundary classification, not a new regular formula or blanket subsumption. Record/output count and normalized algebraic degree receive singly exponential fixed-alphabet bounds from the two sequential raw-fiber calls. The initial sample is bounded in the first sampling extension, the second witness is bounded through the product extension, and rational height receives a separate conservative bound that includes target-coordinate summation. The Wald, exact-coverage, and locally saturated Hausdorff scopes remain unchanged. The GEUVADIS application remains an audit protocol conditional on the graph and recovery of the actual released table, not a new numerical reanalysis.

statement_notes.justification: The theorem bounds the actual two-call raw-fiber engine, treats the initial sample and second-stage witness in their correct algebraic fields, and charges the target-coordinate sum height before the existential call.
statement_notes.gap: Chart counts belong to optional diagnostics, while the initial sample need not lie in the field generated by the sampled target and the second-stage witness.
statement_notes.consumer: Exact implementations receive raw degree two for design A, raw degree three for design B, no chart multiplier, separate initial and second-stage degree bounds, and a rational-height recurrence containing the target-sum increment.
